proposals.evidence: DEDR5517 includes the cooking/heat family with Tulu bēyuni/bēpini and Kannada bē, plus Kurux bi’inā and Malto bice/bite. Belari bī cook (something) is a qualified long-ī member of this family; its vowel differs from neighbouring Tulu ē. The article contains transitive cooking as well as intransitive heating, so no unexpressed causative component is supplied. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR2053 gives Tulu (B-K.) koḷu give/grant; several other article members explicitly mean give to a third person. Belari koḷu matches the full form. Bhat1971 p.119 distinguishes its third-person recipient use from itta, retained as a separate unresolved source record; the installed generic give gloss is preserved. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR2747 gives Kannada sey beauty/merit/propriety and saypu rectitude/propriety/merit. Belari seypɨ beautiful is a qualified comparison with this s-y-p formation: the article supplies both the beauty sense and the -p formation, although not the exact Belari adjective. Preserve e and final ɨ; the whole article, not just its displayed head, is proposed. Inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
